name: OpusClip
editorial: For OpusClip, upload a long webinar containing a few good answers and several sections that depend on earlier context. Review the suggested clips for factual completeness before judging their visual polish. Correct captions, names, and brand terms, and reject any cut that makes an answer sound more certain than it was. Compare the recommended hooks with the audience you actually serve. Track the source minutes used for an ordinary batch of videos and count how many clips survive human review. This produces a more useful cost estimate than counting every automatic suggestion. OpusClip is worth evaluating when your work centers on long-form video clipping. Start with a webinar highlight and a podcast teaser; these two deliverables expose different constraints, so a single polished demo is a poor buying test. For the first, write down the time spent preparing source material, making the initial cut, and correcting mistakes. For the second, repeat the process with a fresh asset rather than reusing a finished template. This gives you a practical comparison of effort across routine and less predictable work. Pay particular attention to clip selection, caption cleanup, and context preservation. Ask a colleague to open the exported result on another device and note any missing captions, clipped audio, font substitution, or awkward pacing. Keep the source file so you can measure how painful a late revision would be. A workflow that feels fast for one person may slow down when another person has to review it. Before paying, check how upload minutes and export permissions fit your source volume. Read the current checkout and license terms directly on the merchant site, since plan names and entitlements can change. Save a dated screenshot of the offer and renewal conditions, then compare the total cost over the period you will actually use the tool. If you are buying for a team, assign one person to test access, permissions, and export ownership. This evaluation is our editorial method, not a claim that a discount is available today.
refund_policy: Check current merchant terms; not independently verified.
